item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-73a6a4f616229fd0","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Transparency International reported that the Democratic Republic of Congo received a CPI 2023 score of 20 and that victims of human-rights violations faced denial of justice; the General Inspectorate of Finance had uncovered numerous public-fund mismanagement and corruption cases, including in several institutions and the president’s office, but justice was slow, especially for politically exposed persons. In July 2023, Tshisekedi expressed dissatisfaction with the judiciary’s performance.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly relevant to 2023; the CPI report was published 30 January 2024 and describes 2023 conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The IGF efforts and judicial performance occurred under Tshisekedi’s presidency; the source attributes his dissatisfaction directly to him.","limitations":["The CPI is a perception index and does not establish personal responsibility for each corruption case.","The source does not specify what corrective measures Tshisekedi adopted after expressing dissatisfaction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d97e06e86fd72564","start_unit":9,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The CTBTO status page lists the Democratic Republic of the Congo as having signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty on 4 October 1996 and ratified it on 28 September 2004.","question_ids":["1B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The legal status predates 2023 but remained applicable during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The record concerns the DRC state’s treaty status; it does not attribute the 1996 signature or 2004 ratification personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The document provides no evidence of Tshisekedi’s 2023 actions concerning CTBT implementation, compliance, or resourcing.","The source is not specific to the ruler’s period except for continuing treaty status."]},{"source_id":"SRC-904016f53c56ea44","start_unit":17,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"After the DRC initially invited an EU mission to observe the 20 December 2023 general elections nationwide, the mission was reduced to an eight-person Electoral Expert Mission based in Kinshasa, operating with the agreement of DRC authorities. It was tasked with technically analyzing the process and issuing findings and recommendations.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election process.","ruler_attribution":"The reduction and agreed operating arrangement are attributed to the DRC authorities, not expressly to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The document does not explain why the full observation mission was reduced.","It does not report the mission’s eventual findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-904016f53c56ea44","start_unit":17,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The EU stated that the 2023 electoral process should be inclusive, free, transparent, and peaceful, with freedom of expression, press, assembly, association, and movement; equal campaigning conditions; independent civil-society observation; and free media access.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.3","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election process.","ruler_attribution":"These were standards and recommendations addressed to all Congolese stakeholders and are not evidence that Tshisekedi implemented them.","limitations":["The statement is normative and does not itself establish compliance or violations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-15e41d783bbb4019","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights reported in December 2022 that insecurity in eastern DRC had escalated because of armed groups including M23, causing massacres, disappearances, displacement, refugee flows, and severe humanitarian consequences. It cited reports that more than one hundred Hutu community members were killed at Kishishe and alleged that M23 imposed taxes, looted and burned property, abducted people, and imposed forced communal labor.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"This is a late-2022 baseline immediately preceding the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The abuses are attributed to armed groups; the Commission separately reminds the DRC of its duty to protect residents, investigate, punish perpetrators, and provide reparations.","limitations":["The document does not establish that Tshisekedi personally ordered or tolerated these specific abuses.","The report predates 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-15e41d783bbb4019","start_unit":15,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The African Commission called on all conflict parties to end hostilities, respect international humanitarian law, pursue dialogue, and implement the 6 December 2022 Nairobi agreement involving the DRC government and 53 armed groups; it urged the M23 to join the process and called on the DRC to protect populations, investigate violations, punish perpetrators, and provide victim reparations.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.7","2B.9","3B.4","3B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The agreement and recommendations were issued in December 2022 and provide context for 2023 conflict management.","ruler_attribution":"The Commission acknowledged efforts by DRC authorities while directing the government to take further protective and accountability measures.","limitations":["The source does not document whether the requested investigations, punishments, or reparations occurred in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c87cdb25e33a70c2","start_unit":16,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In response to an invitation from the DRC Foreign Ministry, the EU deployed an election observation mission for the 20 December 2023 general elections. The mission included 13 core experts, 42 long-term observers, and planned short-term observers, with a mandate to monitor the process against international and regional standards and publish preliminary and final reports with recommendations.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.6","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election process.","ruler_attribution":"The invitation is attributed to the DRC Foreign Ministry; the document does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal role.","limitations":["The document describes the monitoring arrangement, not the election’s final quality or the government’s response to recommendations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4168e2e6f0f7868d","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"At the June 2022 Nairobi process conclave attended by Tshisekedi, heads of state adopted an operational framework, status-of-forces agreement, and rules of engagement for an EAC Regional Force; they directed an immediate ceasefire, withdrawal from recently taken positions, cooperation on disarmament and demobilization, and intensified political consultations with armed groups.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.7","3B.9","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The agreement predates 2023 but was a relevant conflict-management commitment entering the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi attended and the communiqué thanked him for pursuing a regional route to resolve eastern DRC insecurity.","limitations":["The document does not show Tshisekedi’s subsequent implementation or compliance during 2023.","The agreement was multilateral and does not isolate his individual decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4168e2e6f0f7868d","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"The Nairobi communiqué required all parties to cease hate speech, genocide threats, and politically inciting language, and to address refugees, internally displaced persons, combatant reintegration, citizenship, and development through concerted and durable measures.","question_ids":["2B.4","3B.3","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The commitments were made in 2022 and remained relevant to the 2023 conflict.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi was a participating head of state; implementation responsibility was collective.","limitations":["No evidence in this document shows whether the commitments were enforced or achieved in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2e87ee3bc9fe00b3","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The 20 December 2023 National Assembly election was held on its normal legal schedule with full renewal of 500 seats. Tshisekedi’s Sacred Union coalition and allies won 450 of 477 confirmed seats, while he was simultaneously re-elected president with 73 percent in the first round.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.8","8B.5","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 elections.","ruler_attribution":"The results concern Tshisekedi’s re-election and coalition’s legislative majority.","limitations":["The source notes that opposition candidates rejected the results.","The figures were preliminary/subject to disputes and later constitutional review."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2e87ee3bc9fe00b3","start_unit":16,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"The 2023 elections experienced logistical problems: many polling stations opened late, voting extended into a second day, parts of Nord-Kivu did not vote because of conflict, some constituencies were annulled for alleged fraud, and electoral disputes remained pending. Sixty-one women were initially elected to the 477-member legislature, or 12.8 percent.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.7","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 elections.","ruler_attribution":"The problems occurred under Tshisekedi’s administration, but the source does not assign personal responsibility for each logistical or fraud allegation.","limitations":["The source does not identify the causes of every delay or quantify the effect on the presidential result.","Women’s representation is a descriptive outcome, not evidence of a specific Tshisekedi policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-81f19d6288f04288","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The African Union Peace and Security Council reported grave insecurity, humanitarian deterioration, and socio-economic decline in eastern DRC in February 2023, condemned human-rights abuses by M23, ADF, FDLR, and other armed groups, and demanded immediate cessation of hostilities and unconditional withdrawal.","question_ids":["2B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns February 2023 conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The abuses are attributed to armed groups; the Council addressed the DRC government as a party responsible for conflict response and protection.","limitations":["The communiqué does not establish that Tshisekedi personally caused the abuses.","It does not provide outcome data on the government’s response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-81f19d6288f04288","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The AU PSC called for revitalization and implementation of the regional peace framework, M23 cantonment and disarmament under DRC authority with EAC and MONUSCO supervision, rehabilitation and community development for ex-combatants, voluntary return of displaced people and refugees, and cooperation among DRC forces, MONUSCO, and the EAC Regional Force.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.7","2B.9","3B.9","6B.6","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a February 2023 regional response and implementation agenda.","ruler_attribution":"The Council recognized Tshisekedi’s participation and addressed implementation responsibilities to the DRC and regional institutions.","limitations":["The document records recommendations and authorizations, not completed implementation or results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c1c8176152de1c6","start_unit":14,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Tshisekedi was sworn in for a second term after a highly contested 2023 election marked by logistical problems, irregularities, and violence. CENI cancelled results in two constituencies and disqualified 82 candidates, including members of the ruling coalition; the Catholic bishops described the election as an electoral catastrophe involving fraud, corruption, vandalism, and incitement, while the Carter Center attributed at least 19 deaths to election-related violence.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source was published in March 2024 but reports the December 2023 election.","ruler_attribution":"The election occurred under Tshisekedi’s administration and produced his second-term victory; the allegations do not by themselves prove his personal direction.","limitations":["The source presents findings and assessments from multiple observers with differing institutional roles.","It does not establish that Tshisekedi personally ordered electoral fraud or violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c1c8176152de1c6","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that during Tshisekedi’s first term authorities increasingly cracked down on journalists, activists, government critics, and opposition actors, including online. Journalist Stanis Bujakera had been detained since 8 September 2023 in a politically motivated prosecution; security forces repeatedly used unnecessary or excessive force against peaceful demonstrations; and dozens of civilians were killed by Republican Guards in Goma on 30 August 2023, for which HRW called for accountability.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 events and the broader first-term record.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to state authorities and security forces during Tshisekedi’s administration; the source also notes earlier presidential commitments concerning security-agency detention centers.","limitations":["The source does not establish a personal order from Tshisekedi for each detention or use of force.","The death toll is described as dozens without a final adjudicated figure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c1c8176152de1c6","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that more than one million civilians were displaced by fighting involving M23, that the government supported the Wazalendo militia coalition and FDLR to fight alongside Congolese soldiers, contracted hundreds of private military personnel, and acquired armed drones, raising concerns about broader regional escalation. It also reported that more than 100 armed groups remained active and that attacks on displaced-person camps increased in Ituri.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.5","2B.8","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source was published in March 2024 and describes conditions during 2023 and the preceding two years.","ruler_attribution":"HRW attributes support for Wazalendo and FDLR, private military contracting, and military acquisitions to Tshisekedi’s administration.","limitations":["The source is an advocacy report and does not quantify the government’s direct operational control over every aligned group.","Some displacement and armed-group activity predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c1c8176152de1c6","start_unit":17,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that the EAC force left Congo at the end of 2023, SADC troops began deploying in December, and Tshisekedi’s administration requested MONUSCO’s departure by the end of 2024. It also reported that the justice system remained dysfunctional because of corruption, political and military interference, and resource shortfalls; many alleged rights violators remained unpunished; and Tshisekedi publicly acknowledged lack of justice-system progress as a downside to his record and called for reform.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.9","3B.4","3B.6","6B.6","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns late 2023 and the first-term record, with publication in March 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The MONUSCO request and public acknowledgment of justice-system failure are attributed to Tshisekedi’s administration and to Tshisekedi personally, respectively.","limitations":["The source does not show whether requested justice reforms were enacted or effective by the end of 2023.","The EAC withdrawal and SADC deployment were regional developments with multiple causes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c1c8176152de1c6","start_unit":18,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that national consultations on transitional justice occurred during Tshisekedi’s first term, but he had not committed to concrete measures; most atrocities remained unpunished. It also reported that CENI and the Constitutional Court were perceived as politicized, election observers questioned the impartiality and transparency of the December 2023 process, voter turnout fell to a historical low of 43 percent, and reforms to CENI had not resolved its politicization.","question_ids":["3B.4","4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source was published in March 2024 and evaluates the 2023 election and first-term institutional record.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the incomplete transitional-justice commitment and CENI reforms to Tshisekedi’s administration; perceived politicization is an institutional finding rather than proof of personal direction.","limitations":["Perceptions of politicization do not by themselves establish unlawful interference.","The source does not detail every reform measure or its implementation history."]},{"source_id":"SRC-40df62d8ea565ea0","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"By September-October 2023, Tshisekedi announced that he would seek MONUSCO’s departure in December 2023, arguing that the mission had failed to cope with rebellions and armed conflict. In October, the IOM reported a record 6.9 million internally displaced people in the DRC, more than 80 percent in the east.","question_ids":["2B.7","3B.6","3B.9","6B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The peacekeeper-withdrawal request and rationale are attributed directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The displacement figure reflects broad conflict and humanitarian conditions and does not isolate presidential causation.","The source does not assess whether accelerated withdrawal improved or worsened protection."]},{"source_id":"SRC-12b7eb2912b08eac","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The article reported that during Tshisekedi’s tenure the Congolese franc fell from about 1,600 to almost 2,700 per U.S. dollar, high crisis or emergency food insecurity nearly doubled to nearly 26 million people, more than 60 percent of the population lived below $2.15 per day, and about seven million people were internally displaced. It also reported that Tshisekedi introduced free preschool education, but preschool attendance remained about 5 percent and more than 7.5 million children were out of school.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The article was published January 2024 and compares conditions during Tshisekedi’s 2019-2023 tenure.","ruler_attribution":"The currency, welfare, displacement, and education outcomes are reported for Tshisekedi’s tenure; the preschool program is attributed directly to his government.","limitations":["The article does not establish that the reported outcomes were caused by Tshisekedi’s policies rather than external shocks or inherited conditions.","Several figures cover the full tenure rather than 2023 alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-12b7eb2912b08eac","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The article reported that Tshisekedi created the Sacred Union coalition in 2020, moved to place sympathetic judges in the judiciary, and in June 2022 appointed Dieudonné Kamuleta Badibanga as head of the Constitutional Court. It also reported allegations that the court was stacked with people from Tshisekedi’s ethnic group, that journalists critical of him were arrested, and that close advisers associated with alleged corrupt deals were acquitted.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6","7B.4","7B.5","7B.6","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These are pre-2023 institutional and integrity developments relevant to the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The coalition creation and judicial appointment are attributed directly to Tshisekedi; allegations of ethnic stacking and adviser corruption are reported by the article from named or described sources.","limitations":["Several claims are allegations or quotations from political opponents rather than adjudicated findings.","The document does not establish that Tshisekedi personally benefited from each alleged corrupt deal."]},{"source_id":"SRC-12b7eb2912b08eac","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The article reported that the EU’s full election mission was canceled after Congolese secret police refused permits for satellite equipment, leaving eight observers in Kinshasa; election logistics were underprepared, 11,000 polling stations did not open or were not counted, machines malfunctioned or were reportedly taken to private homes, and polling was extended beyond one day. It further reported that CENI invalidated results for 82 legislative candidates, including ruling-coalition members, and faced allegations of failing to account for $400 million in state funds.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 elections and immediate post-election period.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes the mission restriction to secret police and logistical delays to Tshisekedi’s government, while reporting allegations involving CENI and members of his coalition.","limitations":["The article relies partly on interviews and reported allegations rather than final judicial findings.","It does not prove that Tshisekedi personally ordered the mission restriction, polling-station failures, or alleged diversion of funds."]},{"source_id":"SRC-12b7eb2912b08eac","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"After the election, opposition protests were met with tear gas and alleged attacks by a militia claiming ties to Tshisekedi’s party; troops surrounded Moïse Katumbi’s home and prevented him from leaving. The article reported that opposition candidates avoided court challenges because they regarded the courts as controlled by Tshisekedi, while CENI’s results remained disputed.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The events occurred in late December 2023 and January 2024; they bear directly on the 2023 election aftermath.","ruler_attribution":"The alleged militia-party ties and military action occurred under Tshisekedi’s administration; the source does not establish a personal order from him.","limitations":["The militia’s connection to Tshisekedi’s party was disputed.","Some reported events occurred after the target period’s end."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4a85788afe9bc20e","start_unit":15,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"The 2007 DRC-Rwanda communiqué committed both governments to prevent direct or indirect support for armed groups, establish strict border controls, share intelligence, cooperate through verification mechanisms, disarm and repatriate foreign armed groups, bring alleged war-crimes perpetrators to justice, protect civilians, and facilitate humanitarian assistance and refugee return.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.7","2B.9","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6","8B.2"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"This is a historical baseline from 2007, far outside Tshisekedi’s 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The commitments were made by earlier DRC and Rwandan governments, not Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The document cannot establish Tshisekedi’s conduct or performance in 2023.","It is relevant only as inherited regional policy context."]},{"source_id":"SRC-40df62d8ea565ea0","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"CFR reported that M23’s renewed offensive displaced nearly 300,000 Congolese by November 2022; a ceasefire agreed by Angola, Burundi, DRC, and Rwanda was not followed by M23’s withdrawal from captured territory. By the end of January 2023, eastern DRC displacement exceeded 450,000.","question_ids":["2B.7","3B.6","3B.9","6B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The facts span late 2022 and January 2023, providing direct baseline and early-period context.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi’s government was a party to the ceasefire diplomacy, while M23 was responsible for failing to withdraw according to the source.","limitations":["The source does not assess Tshisekedi’s specific implementation of the ceasefire.","The displacement was caused by multiple armed actors."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["Several documents are historical or normative and provide only contextual evidence for 2023 rather than direct ruler-period findings.","No source supplied evidence concerning Félix Tshisekedi’s conduct on nuclear command-and-control, proliferation controls, or AI, cyber, biological, and other catastrophic dual-use safeguards beyond the DRC’s pre-existing CTBT ratification status.","Allegations and institutional perceptions are preserved as reported facts but are not treated as adjudicated findings or personal orders unless the source expressly attributes them to Tshisekedi."]}
